title: CA AB853: California AI Transparency Act.

obligations: A large online platform shall detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(1))

A large online platform shall provide a user interface to disclose the availability of system provenance data that reliably indicates that the content was generated or substantially altered by a GenAI system or captured by a capture device (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2)(A))

The user interface required by Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2) shall make clearly and conspicuously available to users information sufficient to identify the content's authenticity, origin, or history of modification, including whether provenance data is available, the name of the GenAI system or capture device that created or substantially altered the content if applicable, and whether any digital signatures are available (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2)(B))

A large online platform shall allow a user to inspect all available system provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body in an easily accessible manner by direct interface, by allowing download of a version of the content with its attached system provenance data, or by providing a link to the content's system provenance data displayed on an internet website or in another application provided by the large online platform or a third party (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(3))

A capture device manufacturer shall, with respect to any capture device the capture device manufacturer first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028, provide a user with the option to include a latent disclosure in content captured by the capture device that conveys the name of the capture device manufacturer, the name and version number of the capture device that created or altered the content, and the time and date of the content's creation or alteration (Sec. 22757.3.3(a)(1))

A capture device manufacturer shall, with respect to any capture device the capture device manufacturer first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028, embed latent disclosures in content captured by the device by default (Sec. 22757.3.3(a)(2))

A capture device manufacturer shall comply with Section 22757.3.3 only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body (Sec. 22757.3.3(b))
prohibitions: A large online platform shall not, to the extent technically feasible, knowingly strip any system provenance data or digital signature that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body from content uploaded or distributed on the large online platform (Sec. 22757.3.1(b))
A GenAI system hosting platform shall not knowingly make available a GenAI system that does not place disclosures pursuant to Section 22757.3 (Sec. 22757.3.2(a))

Passed 2025-10-13. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This act delays the operative date of the California AI Transparency Act to August 2, 2026. Beginning January 1, 2027, it requires large online platforms to detect and disclose provenance data for distributed content and prohibits them from stripping that data, and it prohibits GenAI hosting platforms from knowingly making available GenAI systems that do not place disclosures. Beginning January 1, 2028, it requires capture device manufacturers to provide a user option for latent disclosures and to embed latent disclosures by default in certain capture devices.

Who it applies to

  • Large online platforms
  • GenAI system hosting platforms
  • Capture device manufacturers
  • Covered providers
  • Third party licensees of covered providers

Effective date

The chapter becomes operative on August 2, 2026 (Sec. 22757.6). Section 22757.3.1 and Section 22757.3.2 become operative on January 1, 2027 (Sec. 22757.3.1(c), Sec. 22757.3.2(b)). Section 22757.3.3 becomes operative on January 1, 2028 (Sec. 22757.3.3(c)).

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence or AI: an engineered or machine based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments (Sec. 22757.1(a))
  • Capture device: a device that can record photographs, audio, or video content, including, but not limited to, video and still photography cameras, mobile phones with built in cameras or microphones, and voice recorders (Sec. 22757.1(b))
  • Capture device manufacturer: a person who produces a capture device for sale in the state; does not include a person exclusively engaged in the assembly of a capture device (Sec. 22757.1(c))
  • Covered provider: a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system that has over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state (Sec. 22757.1(d))
  • Digital signature: a cryptography based method that identifies the user or entity that attests to the information provided in the signed section (Sec. 22757.1(e))
  • Generative artificial intelligence system or GenAI system: an artificial intelligence that can generate derived synthetic content, including text, images, video, and audio, that emulates the structure and characteristics of the system's training data (Sec. 22757.1(f))
  • GenAI hosting platform: an internet website or application that makes available for download the source code or model weights a generative artificial intelligence system by a resident of the state, regardless of whether the terms of that use include compensation (Sec. 22757.1(g))
  • Large online platform: a public facing social media platform, file sharing platform, mass messaging platform, or stand alone search engine that distributes content to users who did not create or collaborate in creating the content that exceeded 2,000,000 unique monthly users during the preceding 12 months; does not include a broadband internet access service as defined in Section 3100 of the Civil Code or a telecommunications service as defined in Section 153 of Title 47 of the United States Code (Sec. 22757.1(h))
  • Latent: present but not manifest (Sec. 22757.1(i))
  • Manifest: easily perceived, understood, or recognized by a natural person (Sec. 22757.1(j))
  • Mass messaging platform: a direct messaging platform that allows users to distribute content to more than 100 users simultaneously (Sec. 22757.1(k))
  • Metadata: structural or descriptive information about data (Sec. 22757.1(l))
  • Personal information: has the same meaning as defined in Section 1798.140 of the Civil Code (Sec. 22757.1(m))
  • Personal provenance data: provenance data that contains either personal information or unique device, system, or service information that is reasonably capable of being associated with a particular user; does not include information contained within a digital signature (Sec. 22757.1(n))
  • Provenance data: data that is embedded into digital content, or that is included in the digital content's metadata, for the purpose of verifying the digital content's authenticity, origin, or history of modification (Sec. 22757.1(o))
  • System provenance data: provenance data that is not reasonably capable of being associated with a particular user and that contains either information regarding the type of device, system, or service that was used to generate a piece of digital content or information related to content authenticity (Sec. 22757.1(p))

Obligations

  • A large online platform shall detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(1))
  • A large online platform shall provide a user interface to disclose the availability of system provenance data that reliably indicates that the content was generated or substantially altered by a GenAI system or captured by a capture device (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2)(A))
  • The user interface required by Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2) shall make clearly and conspicuously available to users information sufficient to identify the content's authenticity, origin, or history of modification, including whether provenance data is available, the name of the GenAI system or capture device that created or substantially altered the content if applicable, and whether any digital signatures are available (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2)(B))
  • A large online platform shall allow a user to inspect all available system provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body in an easily accessible manner by direct interface, by allowing download of a version of the content with its attached system provenance data, or by providing a link to the content's system provenance data displayed on an internet website or in another application provided by the large online platform or a third party (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(3))
  • A capture device manufacturer shall, with respect to any capture device the capture device manufacturer first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028, provide a user with the option to include a latent disclosure in content captured by the capture device that conveys the name of the capture device manufacturer, the name and version number of the capture device that created or altered the content, and the time and date of the content's creation or alteration (Sec. 22757.3.3(a)(1))
  • A capture device manufacturer shall, with respect to any capture device the capture device manufacturer first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028, embed latent disclosures in content captured by the device by default (Sec. 22757.3.3(a)(2))
  • A capture device manufacturer shall comply with Section 22757.3.3 only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body (Sec. 22757.3.3(b))

Prohibitions

  • A large online platform shall not, to the extent technically feasible, knowingly strip any system provenance data or digital signature that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body from content uploaded or distributed on the large online platform (Sec. 22757.3.1(b))
  • A GenAI system hosting platform shall not knowingly make available a GenAI system that does not place disclosures pursuant to Section 22757.3 (Sec. 22757.3.2(a))

Penalties and enforcement

A violator of this chapter is liable for a civil penalty of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per violation, collected in a civil action filed by the Attorney General, a city attorney, or a county counsel (Sec. 22757.4(a)(1)). A prevailing plaintiff in such an action is entitled to all reasonable attorney's costs and fees (Sec. 22757.4(a)(2)). Each day that a covered provider, large online platform, or capture device manufacturer is in violation is deemed a discrete violation (Sec. 22757.4(b)). For a violation by a third party licensee of paragraph (3) of subdivision (c) of Section 22757.3, the Attorney General, a county counsel, or a city attorney may bring a civil action for injunctive relief and reasonable attorney's fees and costs (Sec. 22757.4(c)). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • A large online platform that distributes content must implement detection of provenance data compliant with widely adopted specifications and provide user interface and inspection options, and it cannot knowingly strip compliant system provenance data or digital signatures (Sec. 22757.3.1)
  • A GenAI system hosting platform must ensure that any GenAI system it makes available places disclosures pursuant to Section 22757.3, or it is prohibited from knowingly making that system available (Sec. 22757.3.2)
  • A capture device manufacturer must add latent disclosure options and default embedding for capture devices first produced for sale in California on or after January 1, 2028 (Sec. 22757.3.3)
  • Covered providers, large online platforms, and capture device manufacturers face civil penalties of $5,000 per violation, with each day of violation counted as a discrete violation, enforced by the Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel (Sec. 22757.4)
  • The specific obligations of covered providers under Section 22757.3 are referenced but not set out in this text; however, covered providers are subject to daily civil penalties for violations of the chapter (Sec. 22757.4(b))

Notable exemptions

  • Large online platform does not include a broadband internet access service as defined in Section 3100 of the Civil Code or a telecommunications service as defined in Section 153 of Title 47 of the United States Code (Sec. 22757.1(h)(2))
  • Capture device manufacturer does not include a person exclusively engaged in the assembly of a capture device (Sec. 22757.1(c)(2))
  • A capture device manufacturer shall comply with Section 22757.3.3 only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body (Sec. 22757.3.3(b))
  • A large online platform shall not strip system provenance data or digital signatures only to the extent technically feasible (Sec. 22757.3.1(b))
  • Personal provenance data does not include information contained within a digital signature (Sec. 22757.1(n)(2))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether your organization is a large online platform, GenAI hosting platform, capture device manufacturer, or covered provider under the definitions in Section 22757.1
  • If you are a large online platform, implement detection of provenance data compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body for content distributed on your platform (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(1))
  • If you are a large online platform, provide a user interface that clearly and conspicuously discloses the availability of system provenance data and the required information about content authenticity, origin, or history of modification (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(2))
  • If you are a large online platform, allow users to inspect all available compliant system provenance data through direct interface, download, or link (Sec. 22757.3.1(a)(3))
  • If you are a large online platform, do not knowingly strip compliant system provenance data or digital signatures from content uploaded or distributed on your platform, to the extent technically feasible (Sec. 22757.3.1(b))
  • If you are a GenAI hosting platform, ensure that any GenAI system you make available places disclosures pursuant to Section 22757.3 (Sec. 22757.3.2(a))
  • If you are a capture device manufacturer, for any capture device first produced for sale in California on or after January 1, 2028, provide a user option to include a latent disclosure with the required information and embed latent disclosures by default (Sec. 22757.3.3(a))
  • Ensure compliance only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards setting body for capture device latent disclosures (Sec. 22757.3.3(b))
  • Prepare for civil penalties of $5,000 per violation, with each day of violation counted separately, enforced by the Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel (Sec. 22757.4)

 Assembly Bill
 No. 853 Introduced by Assembly Member Wicks (Principal coauthor: Senator Becker) (Coauthor: Assembly Member Zbur) February 19, 2025 An act to amend Sections 22757.1, 22757.4, and 22757.6 of, and to add Sections 22757.3.1, 22757.3.2, and 22757.3.3 to, the Business and Professions Code, relating to artificial intelligence. LEGISLATIVE COUNSEL'S DIGEST AB 853, Wicks.
 California AI Transparency Act. The California AI Transparency Act requires a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system that has over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state to make available an AI detection tool at no cost to the user that, among other things, allows a user to assess whether image, video, or audio content, or content that is a combination thereof, was created or altered by that person’s generative artificial intelligence system and outputs any system provenance data that is detected in the content. Existing law makes the California AI Transparency Act operative on January 1, 2026. This bill would delay the operation of the California AI Transparency Act until August 2, 2026. This bill would, beginning January 1, 2027,
 additionally require a large online platform, as defined, to, among other things related to the provenance of content on the platform, detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform. The bill would also require, beginning January 1, 2028, a capture device manufacturer, with respect to any capture device the capture device manufacturer
 first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028, to, among other things, provide a user with the option to include a latent disclosure in content captured by the capture device that conveys certain information, including the name of the capture device manufacturer. The bill would define “capture device” to mean a device that can record photographs, audio, or video content, including, but not limited to, video and still photography cameras, mobile phones with built-in cameras or microphones, and voice
 recorders. Existing law requires a covered provider to include a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination thereof, created by the covered provider’s GenAI system that, among other things, conveys certain information and is permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove, to the extent it is technically feasible. This bill would, beginning January 1, 2027, prohibit a GenAI system hosting platform, as defined, from knowingly making available a GenAI system that does not place disclosures, pursuant to those
 provisions. This bill would declare that its provisions are severable. Digest Key

SEC. 2.  Section 22757.3.1 is added to the Business and Professions Code, to read: 22757.3.1.  (a) A large online platform shall do all of the following: (1) Detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established

(B) The name and version number of the capture device that created or altered the content. (C) The time and date of the content’s creation or alteration. (2) Embed latent disclosures in content captured by the device by default. (b) A capture device manufacturer shall comply with this section only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body. (c) This section shall become operative on January 1, 2028. SEC. 5.  Section 22757.4 of the Business and Professions Code is amended to read: 22757.4.  (a) (1) A violator of this chapter shall be liable for a civil penalty in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per violation to be collected in a civil action filed by the Attorney General, a city attorney, or a county counsel. (2) A prevailing plaintiff in an action brought pursuant to this subdivision shall be entitled to all reasonable attorney’s costs and fees. (b) Each day that a covered provider, large online platform, or capture device manufacturer is in violation of this chapter shall be deemed a discrete violation. (c) For a violation by a third-party licensee of paragraph (3) of subdivision (c) of Section 22757.3, the Attorney General, a county counsel, or a city attorney may bring a civil action for both of the following: (1) Injunctive relief. (2) Reasonable attorney’s fees and costs. SEC. 6.  Section 22757.6 of the Business and Professions Code is amended to read: 22757.6.  This chapter shall become operative on August 2, 2026. SEC. 7.  The provisions of this act are severable. If any provision of this act or its application is held invalid, that invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application.
